summary: Front page, lead story "Final Settlement / Plain Language from Truthful James A. Bradley." About 100 Black residents met at Marrow's Hall in West Park on the night of July 21, 1893, to protest signs on Asbury Park pavilions barring Black patrons. Colonel William Murrell, editor of the New Jersey Trumpet, was among the platform speakers arguing for the rights of the race; resort founder James A. Bradley later entered and defended his segregation policy at length, denying he used racial slurs and insisting pavilions were private property.
